passages.text: And calling His twelve disciples to Him, Jesus gave them authority over unclean spirits, so that they could drive them out and heal every disease and sickness.
passages.sermon:
Jesus called His twelve disciples to Him.
Jesus gave His twelve disciples authority over unclean spirits.
The twelve disciples could drive out unclean spirits.
The twelve disciples could heal every disease.
The twelve disciples could heal every sickness.
passages.original: Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος τοὺς δώδεκα μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ἐξουσίαν πνευμάτων ἀκαθάρτων ὥστε ἐκβάλλειν αὐτὰ καὶ θεραπεύειν πᾶσαν νόσον καὶ πᾶσαν μαλακίαν

passages.text: These are the names of the twelve apostles: first Simon, called Peter, and his brother Andrew; James son of Zebedee, and his brother John; Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew the tax collector; James son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus; Simon the Zealot, and Judas Iscariot, who betrayed Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Jesus chose twelve apostles.
Their names are as follows.
The first is Simon, who is called Peter.
Andrew is Peter’s brother.
James is the son of Zebedee.
John is James’s brother.
Philip is one of the twelve.
Bartholomew is also one of the twelve.
Thomas is included among them.
Matthew is a tax collector.
James is the son of Alphaeus.
Thaddaeus is one of the twelve.
Simon the Zealot is also included.
Judas Iscariot is one of the twelve.
Judas Iscariot betrayed Jesus.
passages.original: Τῶν δὲ δώδεκα ἀποστόλων τὰ ὀνόματά ἐστιν ταῦτα πρῶτος Σίμων ὁ λεγόμενος Πέτρος καὶ Ἀνδρέας ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ καὶ Ἰάκωβος ὁ τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου καὶ Ἰωάννης ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ Φίλιππος καὶ Βαρθολομαῖος Θωμᾶς καὶ Μαθθαῖος ὁ τελώνης Ἰάκωβος ὁ τοῦ Ἁλφαίου καὶ Θαδδαῖος Σίμων ὁ Καναναῖος καὶ Ἰούδας ὁ Ἰσκαριώτης ὁ καὶ παραδοὺς αὐτόν

passages.text: These twelve Jesus sent out with the following instructions: “Do not go onto the road of the Gentiles or enter any town of the Samaritans.
passages.sermon:
Jesus had twelve disciples.
Jesus sent these twelve disciples out.
Jesus gave them instructions.
Jesus said, “Do not go onto the road of the Gentiles.
Do not enter any town of the Samaritans.”
passages.original: Τούτους τοὺς δώδεκα ἀπέστειλεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς παραγγείλας αὐτοῖς λέγων Εἰς ὁδὸν ἐθνῶν μὴ ἀπέλθητε καὶ εἰς πόλιν Σαμαριτῶν μὴ εἰσέλθητε

passages.text: Go rather to the lost sheep of Israel.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the twelve apostles.
He gave them instructions.
He told them where to go.
He said, “Go to the lost sheep of Israel.”
The lost sheep of Israel are the people of Israel who have gone astray.
Do not go to other nations.
Do not go to the Samaritans.
Go only to the people of Israel who need help.
Go to those who are lost among God’s people.
Go to them first.
passages.original: πορεύεσθε δὲ μᾶλλον πρὸς τὰ πρόβατα τὰ ἀπολωλότα οἴκου Ἰσραήλ

passages.text: As you go, preach this message: ‘The kingdom of heaven is near.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his twelve disciples.
He sent them out with instructions.
He told them to go.
He told them to preach as they went.
He gave them a message to say.
They must say, “The kingdom of heaven is near.”
passages.original: πορευόμενοι δὲ κηρύσσετε λέγοντες ὅτι Ἤγγικεν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν

passages.text: Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse the lepers, drive out demons. Freely you have received; freely give.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
He gave them instructions.
He told them to heal the sick.
He told them to raise the dead.
He told them to cleanse those who have leprosy.
He told them to drive out demons.
He reminded them that they received these gifts freely.
He commanded them to give freely to others.
passages.original: ἀσθενοῦντας θεραπεύετε νεκροὺς ἐγείρετε λεπροὺς καθαρίζετε δαιμόνια ἐκβάλλετε δωρεὰν ἐλάβετε δωρεὰν δότε

passages.text: Do not carry any gold or silver or copper in your belts.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
\r\nHe sent them out to preach.
\r\nHe gave them instructions.
\r\nHe said, "Do not carry gold in your belts."
\r\nDo not carry silver in your belts.
\r\nDo not carry copper in your belts.
passages.original: Μὴ κτήσησθε χρυσὸν μηδὲ ἄργυρον μηδὲ χαλκὸν εἰς τὰς ζώνας ὑμῶν

passages.text: Take no bag for the road, or second tunic, or sandals, or staff; for the worker is worthy of his provisions.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
\r\nHe sent them out to serve others.
\r\nHe gave them instructions.
\r\nDo not take a bag for your journey.
\r\nDo not take a second tunic.
\r\nDo not take extra sandals.
\r\nDo not take a staff.
\r\nGod will provide for you.
\r\nA worker deserves to receive food and support.
passages.original: μὴ πήραν εἰς ὁδὸν μηδὲ δύο χιτῶνας μηδὲ ὑποδήματα μηδὲ ῥάβδον ἄξιος γὰρ ὁ ἐργάτης τῆς τροφῆς αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Whatever town or village you enter, find out who is worthy there and stay at his house until you move on.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
He sent them to preach in different places.
He told them what to do when they entered a town or village.
When you enter any town or village, look for a worthy person there.
A worthy person welcomes you and supports your mission.
Stay at the house of that worthy person.
Remain there until you leave that place.
passages.original: Εἰς ἣν δ’ ἂν πόλιν ἢ κώμην εἰσέλθητε ἐξετάσατε τίς ἐν αὐτῇ ἄξιός ἐστιν κἀκεῖ μείνατε ἕως ἂν ἐξέλθητε

passages.text: As you enter the home, greet its occupants.
passages.sermon: You are entering a home.\r\nGreet the people who live there.
passages.original: εἰσερχόμενοι δὲ εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν ἀσπάσασθε αὐτήν

passages.text: If the home is worthy, let your peace rest on it; but if it is not, let your peace return to you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus sent his disciples to different towns and villages.
He told them to look for a worthy person in each place.
If the disciples found a worthy home, they should let their peace rest on that home.
If the home was not worthy, the disciples should let their peace return to themselves.
passages.original: καὶ ἐὰν μὲν ᾖ ἡ οἰκία ἀξία ἐλθάτω ἡ εἰρήνη ὑμῶν ἐπ’ αὐτήν ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ᾖ ἀξία ἡ εἰρήνη ὑμῶν πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐπιστραφήτω

passages.text: And if anyone will not welcome you or heed your words, shake the dust off your feet when you leave that home or town.
passages.sermon:
Jesus sent his disciples to preach.
Some people will not welcome you.
Some people will not listen to your words.
If this happens, leave that house or town.
As you leave, shake the dust off your feet.
passages.original: καὶ ὃς ἂν μὴ δέξηται ὑμᾶς μηδὲ ἀκούσῃ τοὺς λόγους ὑμῶν ἐξερχόμενοι ἔξω τῆς οἰκίας ἢ τῆς πόλεως ἐκείνης ἐκτινάξατε τὸν κονιορτὸν τῶν ποδῶν ὑμῶν

passages.text: Truly I tell you, it will be more bearable for Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for that town.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus warned about people who reject His messengers.
Jesus said, “I tell you the truth.”
God judged Sodom and Gomorrah for their great sin.
On the day of judgment, Sodom and Gomorrah will face punishment.
But that town, which rejects you, will face even greater punishment.
It will be easier for Sodom and Gomorrah than for that town on the day of judgment.
passages.original: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ἀνεκτότερον ἔσται γῇ Σοδόμων καὶ Γομόρρων ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως ἢ τῇ πόλει ἐκείνῃ

passages.text: Behold, I am sending you out like sheep among wolves; therefore be as shrewd as snakes and as innocent as doves.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, “I am sending you out.”
You are like sheep.
You are going out among wolves.
Be wise like snakes.
Be innocent like doves.
passages.original: Ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἀποστέλλω ὑμᾶς ὡς πρόβατα ἐν μέσῳ λύκων γίνεσθε οὖν φρόνιμοι ὡς οἱ ὄφεις καὶ ἀκέραιοι ὡς αἱ περιστεραί

passages.text: But beware of men; for they will hand you over to their councils and flog you in their synagogues.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He warned them about people.
People will hand you over to their councils.
They will flog you in their synagogues.
Be careful of men.
passages.original: Προσέχετε δὲ ἀπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων παραδώσουσιν γὰρ ὑμᾶς εἰς συνέδρια καὶ ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς αὐτῶν μαστιγώσουσιν ὑμᾶς

passages.text: On My account, you will be brought before governors and kings as witnesses to them and to the Gentiles.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “You will be brought before governors.
You will be brought before kings.
This will happen because of Me.
You will stand as witnesses to these rulers.
You will also be witnesses to the Gentiles.”
passages.original: καὶ ἐπὶ ἡγεμόνας δὲ καὶ βασιλεῖς ἀχθήσεσθε ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς καὶ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν

passages.text: But when they hand you over, do not worry about how to respond or what to say. In that hour you will be given what to say.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
\r\nHe warned them about persecution.
\r\nHe said, "People will hand you over to authorities."
\r\nWhen this happens, do not worry.
\r\nDo not be anxious about how to answer.
\r\nDo not be anxious about what to say.
\r\nAt that moment, God will give you the words to speak.
passages.original: ὅταν δὲ παραδῶσιν ὑμᾶς μὴ μεριμνήσητε πῶς ἢ τί λαλήσητε δοθήσεται γὰρ ὑμῖν ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ τί λαλήσητε

passages.text: For it will not be you speaking, but the Spirit of your Father speaking through you.
passages.sermon:
You will not be the one who speaks.
The Spirit will speak through you.
The Spirit belongs to your Father.
Your Father's Spirit will speak inside you.
passages.original: οὐ γὰρ ὑμεῖς ἐστε οἱ λαλοῦντες ἀλλὰ τὸ Πνεῦμα τοῦ Πατρὸς ὑμῶν τὸ λαλοῦν ἐν ὑμῖν

passages.text: Brother will betray brother to death, and a father his child; children will rise against their parents and have them put to death.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples about coming persecution.
He said that families will turn against each other.
A brother will betray his brother to death.
A father will betray his child to death.
Children will rise up against their parents.
Children will have their parents put to death.
passages.original: Παραδώσει δὲ ἀδελφὸς ἀδελφὸν εἰς θάνατον καὶ πατὴρ τέκνον καὶ ἐπαναστήσονται τέκνα ἐπὶ γονεῖς καὶ θανατώσουσιν αὐτούς

passages.text: You will be hated by everyone because of My name, but the one who perseveres to the end will be saved.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He warned them about following Him.
People will hate you because you follow Jesus.
They will hate you because of His name.
Everyone will hate you for this reason.
If you keep going until the end, you will be saved.
The one who endures to the end will receive salvation.
passages.original: καὶ ἔσεσθε μισούμενοι ὑπὸ πάντων διὰ τὸ ὄνομά μου ὁ δὲ ὑπομείνας εἰς τέλος οὗτος σωθήσεται

passages.text: When they persecute you in one town, flee to the next. Truly I tell you, you will not reach all the towns of Israel before the Son of Man comes.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He warned them about persecution.
He said, “When people persecute you in one town, leave that town.
Go to another town.
I tell you the truth.
You will not finish visiting all the towns of Israel before the Son of Man comes.”
passages.original: Ὅταν δὲ διώκωσιν ὑμᾶς ἐν τῇ πόλει ταύτῃ φεύγετε εἰς τὴν ἑτέραν ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω ὑμῖν οὐ μὴ τελέσητε τὰς πόλεις τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ ἕως ἂν ἔλθῃ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου

passages.text: A disciple is not above his teacher, nor a servant above his master.
passages.sermon:
A disciple follows a teacher.
A disciple does not stand above the teacher.
A servant serves a master.
A servant does not stand above the master.
passages.original: Οὐκ ἔστιν μαθητὴς ὑπὲρ τὸν διδάσκαλον οὐδὲ δοῦλος ὑπὲρ τὸν κύριον αὐτοῦ

passages.text: It is enough for a disciple to be like his teacher, and a servant like his master. If the head of the house has been called Beelzebul, how much more the members of his household!
passages.sermon:
A disciple follows his teacher.
A disciple should become like his teacher.
A servant follows his master.
A servant should become like his master.
People called the head of the house Beelzebul.
They will call the members of his household even worse names.
If they insult the leader, they will insult his followers even more.
This is enough for the disciple and the servant.
passages.original: ἀρκετὸν τῷ μαθητῇ ἵνα γένηται ὡς ὁ διδάσκαλος αὐτοῦ καὶ ὁ δοῦλος ὡς ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ εἰ τὸν οἰκοδεσπότην Βεελζεβοὺλ ἐπεκάλεσαν πόσῳ μᾶλλον τοὺς οἰκιακοὺς αὐτοῦ

passages.text: So do not be afraid of them. For there is nothing concealed that will not be disclosed, and nothing hidden that will not be made known.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
He told them not to be afraid of those who oppose them.
Nothing remains hidden forever.
Everything that is covered will be revealed.
Everything that is secret will become known.
passages.original: Μὴ οὖν φοβηθῆτε αὐτούς οὐδὲν γάρ ἐστιν κεκαλυμμένον ὃ οὐκ ἀποκαλυφθήσεται καὶ κρυπτὸν ὃ οὐ γνωσθήσεται

passages.text: What I tell you in the dark, speak in the daylight; what is whispered in your ear, proclaim from the housetops.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking to his disciples.
Jesus teaches his disciples.
Jesus tells his disciples important truths.
Jesus sometimes speaks to his disciples in secret or in darkness.
Jesus tells his disciples to speak these truths openly in the light.
Jesus sometimes whispers messages to his disciples privately.
Jesus commands his disciples to proclaim these messages publicly.
Jesus tells his disciples to announce these truths from the housetops.
Jesus wants his disciples to share his teachings boldly and openly.
passages.original: ὃ λέγω ὑμῖν ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ εἴπατε ἐν τῷ φωτί καὶ ὃ εἰς τὸ οὖς ἀκούετε κηρύξατε ἐπὶ τῶν δωμάτων

passages.text: Do not be afraid of those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Instead, fear the One who can destroy both soul and body in hell.
passages.sermon:
Do not be afraid of people who can kill your body.
They cannot kill your soul.
Do not fear them.
Fear God instead.
God can destroy both your soul and your body in hell.
passages.original: Καὶ μὴ φοβεῖσθε ἀπὸ τῶν ἀποκτεννόντων τὸ σῶμα τὴν δὲ ψυχὴν μὴ δυναμένων ἀποκτεῖναι φοβεῖσθε δὲ μᾶλλον τὸν δυνάμενον καὶ ψυχὴν καὶ σῶμα ἀπολέσαι ἐν γεέννῃ

passages.text: Are not two sparrows sold for a penny? Yet not one of them will fall to the ground apart from the will of your Father.
passages.sermon: Two sparrows cost only a penny.\r\nGod is your Father.\r\nNot one sparrow falls to the ground without your Father’s will.
passages.original: Οὐχὶ δύο στρουθία ἀσσαρίου πωλεῖται καὶ ἓν ἐξ αὐτῶν οὐ πεσεῖται ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἄνευ τοῦ Πατρὸς ὑμῶν

passages.text: And even the very hairs of your head are all numbered.
passages.sermon:
God knows you completely.
God knows every detail about you.
God has counted all the hairs on your head.
Nothing about you is hidden from God.
passages.original: ὑμῶν δὲ καὶ αἱ τρίχες τῆς κεφαλῆς πᾶσαι ἠριθμημέναι εἰσίν

passages.text: So do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.
passages.sermon:
God is your Father.
God cares for you.
You are valuable to God.
You are worth more than many sparrows.
Do not be afraid.
passages.original: μὴ οὖν φοβεῖσθε πολλῶν στρουθίων διαφέρετε ὑμεῖς

passages.text: Therefore everyone who confesses Me before men, I will also confess him before My Father in heaven.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to His followers.
He says this to those who believe in Him.
If anyone confesses Jesus before other people, Jesus will confess that person before His Father in heaven.
Jesus will speak for that person to God the Father.
passages.original: Πᾶς οὖν ὅστις ὁμολογήσει ἐν ἐμοὶ ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων ὁμολογήσω κἀγὼ ἐν αὐτῷ ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ Πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς

passages.text: But whoever denies Me before men, I will also deny him before My Father in heaven.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to His disciples.
Jesus is the Son of God.
He warns about denying Him.
If anyone denies Jesus before other people, Jesus will deny that person.
Jesus will deny that person before His Father.
His Father is in heaven.
passages.original: ὅστις δ’ ἂν ἀρνήσηταί με ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἀρνήσομαι κἀγὼ αὐτὸν ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ Πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς

passages.text: Do not assume that I have come to bring peace to the earth; I have not come to bring peace, but a sword.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to His followers.
Jesus is the subject.
Jesus says, “Do not assume I have come to bring peace to the earth.”
Jesus says, “I have not come to bring peace.”
Jesus says, “I have come to bring a sword.”
passages.original: Μὴ νομίσητε ὅτι ἦλθον βαλεῖν εἰρήνην ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν οὐκ ἦλθον βαλεῖν εἰρήνην ἀλλὰ μάχαιραν

passages.text: For I have come to turn ‘a man against his father, a daughter against her mother, a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking.
Jesus says why He has come.
Jesus says, “I have come to bring division.”
I have come to turn a man against his father.
I have come to turn a daughter against her mother.
I have come to turn a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.
passages.original: ἦλθον γὰρ διχάσαι Ἄνθρωπον κατὰ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ Καὶ θυγατέρα κατὰ τῆς μητρὸς αὐτῆς Καὶ νύμφην κατὰ τῆς πενθερᾶς αὐτῆς

passages.text: A man’s enemies will be the members of his own household.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking to His disciples.
Jesus warns about division.
A man will have enemies.
These enemies will be from his own household.
Family members will oppose him.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐχθροὶ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου οἱ οἰκιακοὶ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Anyone who loves his father or mother more than Me is not worthy of Me; anyone who loves his son or daughter more than Me is not worthy of Me; and anyone who does not take up his cross and follow Me is not worthy of Me.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to His followers.
Jesus says, “If you love your father more than Me, you are not worthy of Me.”
“If you love your mother more than Me, you are not worthy of Me.”
“If you love your son more than Me, you are not worthy of Me.”
“If you love your daughter more than Me, you are not worthy of Me.”
“If you do not take up your cross and follow Me, you are not worthy of Me.”
passages.original: Ὁ φιλῶν πατέρα ἢ μητέρα ὑπὲρ ἐμὲ οὐκ ἔστιν μου ἄξιος καὶ ὁ φιλῶν υἱὸν ἢ θυγατέρα ὑπὲρ ἐμὲ οὐκ ἔστιν μου ἄξιος καὶ ὃς οὐ λαμβάνει τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀκολουθεῖ ὀπίσω μου οὐκ ἔστιν μου ἄξιος

passages.text: Whoever finds his life will lose it, and whoever loses his life for My sake will find it.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to His disciples.
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus says, “Whoever finds his life will lose it.”
If a person tries to keep his life for himself, he will lose it.
Jesus also says, “Whoever loses his life for My sake will find it.”
If a person gives up his life for Jesus, he will find true life.
passages.original: ὁ εὑρὼν τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἀπολέσει αὐτήν καὶ ὁ ἀπολέσας τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ εὑρήσει αὐτήν

passages.text: He who receives you receives Me, and he who receives Me receives the One who sent Me.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to His twelve disciples.\r\nJesus said, “Anyone who receives you receives Me.\r\nAnyone who receives Me receives the One who sent Me.”
passages.original: Ὁ δεχόμενος ὑμᾶς ἐμὲ δέχεται καὶ ὁ ἐμὲ δεχόμενος δέχεται τὸν ἀποστείλαντά με

passages.text: Whoever receives a prophet because he is a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward, and whoever receives a righteous man because he is a righteous man will receive a righteous man’s reward.
passages.sermon:
A prophet is a person who speaks God’s message.
A righteous man is a person who lives according to God’s will.
If you welcome a prophet because he is a prophet, you will receive a prophet’s reward.
If you welcome a righteous man because he is a righteous man, you will receive a righteous man’s reward.
passages.original: ὁ δεχόμενος προφήτην εἰς ὄνομα προφήτου μισθὸν προφήτου λήμψεται καὶ ὁ δεχόμενος δίκαιον εἰς ὄνομα δικαίου μισθὸν δικαίου λήμψεται

passages.text: And if anyone gives even a cup of cold water to one of these little ones because he is My disciple, truly I tell you, he will never lose his reward.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “If anyone gives a cup of cold water to one of these little ones,
and he does this because the person is My disciple,
I tell you the truth,
that person will never lose his reward.”
passages.original: καὶ ὃς ἂν ποτίσῃ ἕνα τῶν μικρῶν τούτων ποτήριον ψυχροῦ μόνον εἰς ὄνομα μαθητοῦ ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν οὐ μὴ ἀπολέσῃ τὸν μισθὸν αὐτοῦ
